candidates.desc: A retro cartoon office worker taps a stack of pages, staples them with his red stapler, then faces an absurdly tall tower of paper; he reloads the stapler with fresh staples, works through the pile and triumphantly lifts the stapled stack overhead.
In an electronics store a woman compares two boxed headphones, unboxes and tries on the white pair with delight, then takes them to the counter where the cashier bags them and she pays by card.

By candlelight two women fold a handwritten letter and slide it into a cream paper envelope. They drip red sealing wax on the flap, press a stamp into it and admire the sealed envelope, one giving it a kiss.

An animated jeweler in a plum suit lifts a heavy gold bar onto her counter, polishes it until it shines and admires her reflection in it, then drapes a gold chain and slips on gold bangles, hugging the bar possessively.

A courier in a yellow vest hands a surprised red-haired woman a brown paper parcel tied with string at her garden gate; she carries it to the front door, shakes it curiously while a man watches, then opens the box and pulls out the tissue-wrapped contents excitedly.

In a hand-painted village grocery, a cashier rings up a man's basket of fruit and the old register prints an endless receipt that spirals around his body; he studies the huge list, then rolls it up and pockets it.

On a sunny Indian street, a man peels one flower stamp off a full sheet, sticks it onto the corner of an envelope, and a woman then drops the letter into a red pillar postbox with a crow perched on top.

A man draws a lunchbox inside a heart on a pink sticky note, peels it off the pad and presses it onto the fridge door; his partner comes home, spots the pink square, smiles, and opens the fridge to find the packed lunchbox waiting.

In a hand-painted anime town, a woman's brown wallet slips out of her bag onto the cobblestones. A man on a bicycle spots it, picks it up, checks the cards and coins inside and rides after her to return it at the fountain; she thanks him with a flower.

Outside a hotel at night a young man in a yellow shirt is caught fiddling with the silver hood ornament of a light-blue Rolls-Royce; warned off-camera that the car is so expensive — about 400 grand — his eyes go wide, he points at the ornament in disbelief, then leans down and strokes the hood, apologizing to the car.

A couple walk hand in hand down the bright marble concourse of a shopping mall, she in a short gold dress and he in a white t-shirt and shorts. She stops in front of a lit shop window full of long evening gowns on mannequins and pulls him back towards it. Her face fills the frame with a hopeful, pleading look; his face follows, tight-lipped and reluctant. In the last shot the two of them walk out of the shop again, both loaded down with big paper carrier bags in each hand.

A black cat in a red apron works behind a street hot dog stand while a husky stands at the grill behind it turning sausages with tongs. A customer's hand holds a turquoise bank card out to the card reader on the counter. The cat lays a sausage into a long bun, then squeezes a zigzag of ketchup along it from a red bottle, and finally lifts the finished hot dog up to the camera.

A woman in a beige trench coat walks through flats one after another. First a cramped room with a bed pushed against the wall, a boiler above it, a radiator and a small cooker by a narrow window. Then a small living room with a grey sofa and a balcony door, where she sits down and the caption 1,200 EUR appears over her. Finally she stands in a vast empty glass-walled floor high above a city, turning to look around with her mouth open as the caption 10,000 EUR appears.

A woman in a beige blazer pushes a card into the slot of a cash machine on a busy street, then keys something in. The clip cuts to her walking up to a row of cash machines inside a bright hall, each set into the wall under its own lit sign, and then to a longer row of machines with different bank logos above them where travellers with suitcases stand waiting to use them. Finally she stands in front of one of the machines fanning a thick stack of banknotes in both hands, mouth open in delight.

A price comparison of three beds. First a caption reading €50 over a bare mattress lying on the carpet, where a young man flops down and curls up on it. Then €800 over an ordinary double bed with a colourful patterned duvet, where a woman sits up smiling. Finally €20,000 over a huge four-poster bed in a dark red room, where a man in a silk robe throws himself backwards onto the covers.

A three-part comparison shot on a suburban street. A young man in a hoodie and jeans leans proudly on the roof of a rusty old brown car while the caption 500 EUR sits over it. Cut to a woman in a business suit unlocking a clean silver saloon, captioned 20,000 EUR. Cut to a red Ferrari with both butterfly doors standing wide open, and a man in a tailored suit strolling up to it, captioned 500,000 EUR.

A busy street market. A moustached stallholder in a shirt and waistcoat stands behind a huge pyramid of peaches and holds one up to a young customer, turning it in his fingers to show it off. The customer leans in over the fruit. The vendor then piles peaches into a cardboard box and hands it across the stall. Brass hanging scales sway above the display, other stalls and shoppers fill the street behind.

In a busy public office a young woman with long red hair stands at a service counter, gasps with excitement and picks up a small plastic card that has just been issued to her. She turns it over, reads it, then holds it up beside her face so the photo on the card and her own face are seen together, gives a thumbs up, and the people waiting behind her clap.

Three kitchens are compared with a price caption over each one. First a frail old man stirs a pot on a single gas burner in a shabby room with peeling walls, captioned 500 euro. Then a woman in a bright white family kitchen pulls a tray of cookies out of the oven, captioned 10,000 euro. Last a man stands at the marble island of a glass-walled penthouse kitchen with the city skyline behind him, captioned 100,000 euro.

Three cooks in three very different kitchens. An old man in a vest tastes soup from a wooden spoon over a battered pot on a gas ring in a tiled, run-down room, then cracks an egg into it. A woman in a bright white kitchen lifts a baked cheesy dish out of the oven with oven gloves. Finally a man in a black turtleneck tosses peppers in a frying pan in a penthouse kitchen with copper pans hanging overhead and the night skyline in the windows, then spreads his arms wide.

A young man in a navy hoodie stands at a black roadside mailbox with its red flag up and pulls the front hatch open; the box is empty. A postal worker in a blue jacket and cap arrives and pushes a thick block of white envelopes and a brown parcel into the box, filling it completely. The man reaches back in, drags out the enormous stack of letters and holds it against his chest, mouth open in delight.

A young man in an airport holds an open passport towards the camera and fans the pages: every page is plain white, with nothing on it. He grins, then hands the passport across an immigration counter where an officer's stamp and a screen sit. Later, at a table, he opens the same passport to show pages now crowded with coloured entry stamps and visas, before flicking through it again.

A young woman in a coral jacket rides a stand-up electric scooter along a sunlit seaside promenade, grinning at the camera with the blue sea and a stone breakwater behind her. She then stands beside a long rank of parked rental e-scooters at the water's edge, tapping her phone; a close-up over her shoulder shows the rental app open on the screen with a circular logo and a blue button. Finally a wide shot shows a palm-lined promenade with a dozen people riding hired e-scooters past the trees.

A woman in a grey blazer and glasses sits at her desk in a large open-plan office and looks down in surprise: a takeaway coffee cup and a wrapped pastry have appeared next to her keyboard. She picks up a small white card propped against them and holds it up — a smiley face is drawn on it in pen. She looks around over the top of her monitor at the rows of cubicles where her colleagues are working, then stands holding the coffee, scanning the room to work out who left it. She ends up back at her desk with the cup in both hands, smiling.

Outdoors in a sunny garden full of palms, a young woman in a teal blazer and a young man in a grey suit sit side by side at a long wooden table, each with an open document folder in front of them. A crowd of colleagues in business clothes stands packed behind their chairs. Two small desk flags, one teal and one orange, sit at the front edge of the table. Both sign their documents, the colleagues clap, and then the two stand up and shake hands.

A close shot shows a man's hands sliding a blue-green card out of a brown leather wallet beside a payment terminal with a glowing green ring in a shop. He looks up and smiles, holding the open wallet. At an open-air market he hands the card across crates of oranges, apples and plums to the stallholder while holding a paper bag. Then, over a wooden table, he holds a small brown coin purse upside down and a stream of coins pours out of it into a spreading heap. In the last shot he pushes the coins apart with one finger, sorting the copper and silver pieces on the table while the empty purse hangs in his other hand.

Inside a bank vault lit by ceiling lights, a young man in a white shirt and navy waistcoat holds a bundle of banknotes over a long metal drawer pulled out from a wall of small numbered steel safe deposit boxes. A young woman in a burgundy jumper stands beside him holding a small key. He puts the money into the drawer, slides it back into the wall and turns a key in the small door, while she stands behind him. A huge round vault door stands open in the background.

Inside a busy post office, a young woman in a mustard rain jacket bends over the counter and writes in the little boxes of a long paper form with a pen, concentrating hard as she moves down the page. The view moves closer to her. Behind her a queue of people in winter coats waits with parcels, and clerks serve customers at numbered counter windows. A self-service machine, racks of greeting cards, posters and a wall clock fill the room.

A small café with pale wooden walls. A young woman with long red curly hair in a blue top tips a big glass jar full of copper coins onto the wooden counter, and the small coins pour out into a pile. Behind the counter a white goat in a green apron stands on its hind legs holding a wooden spatula, looks at the pile and then turns to her, and she smiles at it. A paper coffee cup, cinnamon buns under a glass dome, a coffee machine, mugs on a shelf and a plant are around them.

An old-style diner with a long white counter, red stools and pink and blue neon signs on the wall. A customer, seen only by his arms, holds a fan of green dollar bills, and more one-dollar bills lie on the counter in front of him. A smiling young waitress in a beige apron pushes a plate with a slice of cherry pie towards him, picks up a dollar bill from the counter and stands back holding it, smiling. A milkshake and a covered cake stand are on the counter.
